steps.description: Amend plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh: in claim_coordinator_claim, delete the `local our_label="claimed:${machine}"` line and all per-machine label logic; replace with `local label="zbuild:claimed"` and use it throughout; do the same in claim_coordinator_release; add holder extraction from run-status comment on claim conflict; ensure NO `source` of core/claim/claim.sh appears anywhere in plugin.sh (the dependency arrow is claim.sh→plugin.sh, not the reverse; a reverse source creates a circular load)

Update plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/README.md: remove all references to claimed:<machine>; describe the single shared label zbuild:claimed; update ZBUILD_CLAIM_MACHINE_ID row to note it now affects only the holder string in the run-status comment, not the label name
Edit scripts/lib/run-status-render.sh: add <!-- zbuild-holder: CI_URL --> (CI) or <!-- zbuild-holder: run_id=X machine=H --> (local) in rsc_render_header after the run_id marker printf

Create core/claim/claim.sh: thin wiring bridge; source plugin.sh using $_ZBUILD_ROOT (not $(cd ...) subshell); zbuild_claim_build_holder uses ${HOSTNAME} bash variable (not external hostname); zbuild_claim_acquire calls _ccgl_read_labels/_ccgl_add_label/_ccgl_read_holder; zbuild_claim_acquire sanitizes the holder string from _ccgl_read_holder (strip ANSI codes and backslash sequences via printf '%s') before storing in _ZBUILD_CLAIM_HOLDER; zbuild_claim_acquire logs a stderr warning when graceful-degrading on backend error; zbuild_claim_release MUST call `unset _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED` BEFORE `_ccgl_remove_label` (makes second call a no-op — required for DSCLA-13)
Register pipeline.refused.claimed in config/event-schema.json following the pattern of pipeline.refused.issue_locked
Add core/claim/claim.sh to config/shape-change-paths.txt so future changes to the claim bridge trigger the shape floor

Wire core/claim/claim.sh into runner.sh: source at top; call zbuild_claim_build_holder before sidecar spawn; call zbuild_claim_acquire after zbuild_issue_lock_acquire; on refusal emit event + print holder via `printf '%s\n' "$holder"` (not error(), which uses echo -e and would interpret backslash sequences in an attacker-controlled holder) + return 1; call zbuild_claim_release in _runner_abort_trap with declare -F guard, placed AFTER the trap '' INT TERM guard; in both early-failure return paths after zbuild_claim_acquire succeeds but before the EXIT trap is installed (_runner_enter_worktree failure and zbuild_run_branch_setup failure), add `zbuild_claim_release || true` and `zbuild_issue_lock_release || true` before returning, alongside the existing `zbuild_run_cap_release || true`

Amend docs/adr/ADR-005-claim-coordinator.md: extend the existing ## Enforced by §1 bullet to add §1(c) enforcement: claim-coordinator-unit-test.sh [DSCLA-3] (refused: non-zero exit, no stage dispatched, event emitted) and teardown-repeat-signal-test.sh [DSCLA-9] (refused output names holder); add [DSCLA-12] to the §2 bullet alongside [DSCLA-2] for the CI holder rendering case

Amend docs/adr/ADR-059-issue-vs-run-keying.md: add an Enforced by entry for the §4 cross-machine exclusion statement — naming [DSCLA-3] (a run is refused when another machine holds zbuild:claimed on the issue)
